claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified now based on aggregate launch-readiness evidence, despite an acknowledged evaluation gap for the named deployment context of zoning exception explanation.
decision_criteria: General readiness evidence can support launch readiness but does not by itself satisfy model-card certification requirements for named deployment contexts.
Clean certification requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for material evaluation gaps in named launch use cases.
Overstated coverage statements weigh against compliance when the record already identifies unknowns.
evidence_requests: Final model card or certification artifact showing explicit disclosure of the zoning exception explanation evaluation gap.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if any, covering launch with missing evaluations for that named deployment context.
Completed evaluation results for zoning exception explanation, if they now exist.
Release decision record showing whether certification is limited to launch readiness only or includes model-card completeness for named deployment contexts.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a named deployment context, zoning exception explanation, lacks completed evaluations in the packet.
The policy requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The draft model-card statement overstates coverage by treating missing evaluations as if there were no known limitations.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure has been made in the certification artifact.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering the missing named-context evaluations.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify_model is not fully supported because the required disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate for the named evaluation gap is unresolved.
Any implication of clean certification for complete deployment-context coverage is unsupported by the packet.
Any implication that missing evaluations can be treated as passed is contradicted by the QA position in the admissible record.
